Subject: Security exhibit / audit rights for MSA + Order Form

Hi Jonas / Laura —

Thanks for the call earlier. We're packaging the MSA + order form for Helix Health's infosec review and have a few concrete asks so we can hit procurement timelines:

- SOC 2: we need your most recent SOC 2 Type II report (covering Reasonable Controls) and an expected cadence for future attestations.
- Pen test: Helix requires an annual external penetration test and a one-week staging window for sampling. Can we confirm whether Redwood will allow an auditor to run a customer-owned pentest or if you provide a pen-test report? Also need a short statement on whether safe-harbor / remediation periods apply.
- Audit rights: We prefer limited inspection language (scope-limited, non-disruptive, mutually agreed windows) and clear evidence-delivery SLAs (10 business days for supporting artifacts where possible).

Attached is our standard security questionnaire for reference (I removed a couple of items we flagged as out-of-scope). Please send proposed redlines to the security exhibit and order form so our procurement team can review.

Thanks — can we aim to exchange drafts by EOD Tuesday?

—Angela

Thanks Angela — good clarity. Quick response and next steps below (reply inline-ish):

> - SOC 2: we need your most recent SOC 2 Type II report (covering Reasonable Controls) and an expected cadence for future attestations.

We will upload our latest SOC 2 Type II (2026 report) to the Drive folder linked below and include a short cover note describing scope/period. We run annual attestations; next report expected Q2 2028.

> - Pen test: Helix requires an annual external penetration test and a one-week staging window for sampling. Can we confirm whether Redwood will allow an auditor to run a customer-owned pentest or if you provide a pen-test report? Also need a short statement on whether safe-harbor / remediation periods apply.

Proposed approach: Redwood provides an annual third-party pen-test report we commission; for customer-directed tests we allow scoped access under an agreed ops-runbook and signed SOW (staging only, no production impact). We propose 14-day remediation window before any findings are considered final and a mutually-agreed scheduling blackout for high-traffic dates. See attached draft redlines and the pen-test scoping spreadsheet.

> - Audit rights: We prefer limited inspection language (scope-limited, non-disruptive, mutually agreed windows) and clear evidence-delivery SLAs (10 business days for supporting artifacts where possible).

Agree on limited inspection. Our draft adds: (a) sampling approach (logs & configs only, not full code/PII), (b) certified third-party auditors only, (c) 10-business-day evidence turnaround where data exists centrally. Legal may push back on some phrasing.

Attachments: redwood_security_exhibit_draft.docx, pen-test-scoping.xlsx

Proposed next steps:
- Laura to provide legal redlines by EOD Monday.
- I'll circulate a combined exhibit to Helix procurement for review on Tuesday.
- If acceptable, schedule a 30m ops alignment call to lock pen-test window (proposed Wed).

If that timeline works for you, I'll set a calendar invite.

Subject: Re: Security exhibit / audit rights for MSA + Order Form

Thanks — I reviewed the draft and flagged a few items. High level: we're aligned on limited inspection and evidence SLAs but need tighter language around scope, auditor qualifications, and data handling. Key legal redlines below (summary):

1) Scope limitation: Audit rights limited to security controls supporting the Service and associated logs/configuration artifacts; Helix may not inspect application source code or production customer data.
2) Auditor qualification: must be an independent, certified firm (ISO 27001 audit experience preferred). Any auditor selection requires Redwood approval (not to be unreasonably withheld).
3) Notice and scheduling: 30 days' notice for pen test windows; emergency/incident-driven inspections allowed with 48-hour notice and escalation to Redwood security lead.
4) Remediation and safe harbor: findings will be shared in report, Redwood will have 14 business days to remediate high/critical items before customer remediation notices are finalized.
5) Evidence delivery SLA: 10 business days for existing logs/aggregates; for archived or scoped artifacts, up to 20 business days. Where required, we will provide redacted artifacts to protect other customers.
6) Data handling & confidentiality: cross-reference NDA and include vendor-assisted redaction process.

I attached a marked-up redline with concrete clause text. I'm comfortable conceding the 10-business-day target for most items if Helix agrees to the auditor qualification and the safe harbor remediation window.

Attachment: legal_redlines_security_exhibit.docx
